sentinel_issue: The reported inventory violates the documented quotas: 46,522 rooms exceed the 5,120-room cap by over ninefold, while 2,753,430 notes exceed the 163,840 global note cap by roughly 17×, indicating that enforcement or aggregation is not reflecting the stated limits.
worker_response: The apparent violation is an aggregation mismatch: the latest capacities are exactly 32× the documented limits (163,840 = 32×5,120; 5,242,880 = 32×163,840), so 46,522 rooms and 2,753,430 notes are below the aggregate ceilings at 28% and 53%, respectively. Fix the inventory report to label namespace/shard scope and show per-namespace maxima; if this is intended to represent one namespace, enforce the 5,120/163,840 limits at that boundary rather than comparing totals across 32 namespaces.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The arithmetic is correct—46,522/163,840 is 28.4% and 2,753,430/5,242,880 is 52.5%, with capacities 32× the documented limits—but the observations do not establish 32 namespaces or shards, so aggregation mismatch is unproven; scope labeling and per-namespace data are still required.
